title: The Subject, Its Biology, and the Chronic Recurrent Cystitis
case_prompt:
A 52-year-old housewife reports a 12-year history of recurrent cystitis for which she has taken a different antibiotic each month, together with repeated bladder flushes, without lasting relief. She describes episodes of urinary frequency (pollakiuria), a terminal burning sensation when voiding, recurrent gross hematuria, constant bladder pressure, and dysuria. On some occasions, midstream urine and vaginal swabs grew Escherichia coli and Enterococci.

Her medical history is notable for episodes of depression since puberty, first diagnosed at age 48; she completed 50 hours of behavioral therapy and currently takes antidepressants. Her mother also had a history of depression.

Urological evaluation included urine cultures from a catheter, which were sometimes sterile and sometimes positive for E. coli. Renal and bladder sonography showed no abnormalities and no postvoid residual. Transvaginal urethrocystoscopy revealed a normal urethral meatus, bladder mucosa, and ureteral orifices, with no cystocele. Micturating cystourethrography demonstrated a normally configured bladder without vesicoureteral reflux. An excretory urogram was normal, and abdominal and pelvic CT showed only uterine fibroids, with no evidence of fistula.

Psychological assessment noted inhibited gestures and facial expressions, a depressive affect, high motivation, an insecure personality structure, and compulsive defense mechanisms, with a high level of personality organization.
diagnostic_reasoning:
1. Chronic recurrent bacterial cystitis — “At times, the symptoms were ‘determined’ to be a bacterial pollakiuria and dysuria accompanied by evidence of bacteria in the urine and vaginal swabs, which mostly consisted of Escherichia coli and Enterococci.”  
2. Anatomic or functional urinary abnormality — “The urological examination and urodynamics did not reveal any irregularities other than a hypertonic bladder. A subsequent meatotomy did not improve the symptoms.”  
3. Sample contamination of midstream urine — “it was believed that the bacteria originated from anal and vaginal contamination of the midstream urine sample, which was further substantiated when a urine sample collected from a catheter (with the same clinical symptoms) showed no pathological findings.”  
4. Somatoform autonomic dysfunction of the urogenital tract — “It was therefore assumed that the patient suffered from a somatoform autonomic dysfunction of the urogenital tract in addition to a chronic recurrent bacterial cystitis, a finding that also corresponds with the psychological symptoms.”
final_diagnosis: Somatoform autonomic dysfunction of the urogenital system
